subject.title: Dashboard shows deployment version drift warning

question: Should the dashboard treat frontend/backend SHA mismatches after intentional partial deploys as an actionable red alert, a lower-severity informational state, or no visible warning?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally warn on any unequal present SHAs, while the deploy workflow also supports partial targets that can make drift expected.

options.title: Downgrade expected partial drift
options.body: Keep drift detection but change severity, copy, docs, and tests so known partial deploy skew is not presented as a hard warning.

options.title: Keep strict red alert
options.body: Require coordinated same-SHA production stamping and treat every mismatch as an operator-actionable deployment problem.

options.title: Suppress visible drift banner
options.body: Hide mismatch warnings from the dashboard and rely on deploy validation or logs instead, accepting weaker browser-visible skew detection.

recommendation.title: Downgrade expected partial drift
recommendation.body: Keep drift detection but change severity, copy, docs, and tests so known partial deploy skew is not presented as a hard warning.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest current-line routing candidate for the banner, deploy spec, and deploy workflow snapshot that current main and v0.23.1 carry.
